source_signals: Human owner reframed DFMS as replacing outsourcing firms such as TCS or Infosys with a dark-factory agent swarm
Human owner required client check-ins, token budget SWAGs, approvals, change management, and iterative delivery
Prior hardening focused on artifact evidence but did not fully encode the client/vendor engagement layer
goal: Make DFMS an outsourcing-grade client/dark-factory engagement model with governed token budgets, checkpoints, iteration approvals, and change-control gates.

product_specific: No product-specific behavior is introduced; this hardens all governed DFMS engagements.
factory_reusable: Every governed run must establish client owner, delivery owner, rough token SWAG, checkpoint cadence, iteration approvals, and change-control reapproval triggers.
meta_meta_governance: Pass 31 is governed by Attractor, control graph, work ledger, refinery gate, and hardening-runner evidence.

selected_skills.reason: encode the meta-meta engagement goal and token budget requirement
block material factory work without engagement governance
own client checkpoints, rough token SWAGs, iterations, and change approvals
surface token and change-state during client/agent handoffs
turn iterative feedback into approved change requests with token impact

gates: system design and lifecycle include engagement governance and token budget checkpoints

node_contract.what: Encode outsourcing-grade engagement governance and token-budget approval into DFMS.
node_contract.why: The dark factory must feel safer than a human outsourcing firm by making scope, budget, checkpoints, iteration, and change control explicit.
node_contract.how: Add engagement governance template, validator, fixture, runner checks, skill instructions, and design/lifecycle updates.
node_contract.where: df-governance-mayor, df-meta-attractor, dark-factory-orchestrator, df-human-agent-handoff, df-feedback-learning, design docs, and validation suite.
node_contract.when: Before future governed DFMS runs spend material tokens or start iterations.
node_contract.who: Codex as responsible fixer; human owner as client/product owner in the engagement model.
node_contract.how_good: Approved engagement fixture passes while draft/template, missing budget approval, and incomplete change-control fixtures reject.

expert_debate.system_theorist: The dark factory needs a client/vendor control loop above artifact generation so token spend and iteration do not become uncontrolled recursion.
expert_debate.requirements_governance_architect: An outsourcing-grade run needs engagement charter, checkpoint cadence, token budget approval, iteration approvals, and change-request impact analysis.
expert_debate.verification_safety_critic: The requirement must be executable; a validator must reject unapproved budgets, missing checkpoint approvals, and incomplete change-control fields.
expert_debate.synthesis: Install engagement governance as a first-class governance gate before material DFMS execution.

human_decisions: Human owner clarified the meta-meta goal and required token budget negotiation plus approvals for change management and iterations.
assumptions: Token budgets are rough SWAGs, not precise billing estimates.
Approval timestamps in validation fixtures are evidence placeholders for the validator, not real external signatures.
risks: Validator proves structure and approval fields, not actual client satisfaction.
Runtime UI for live token tracking remains future work.
evidence_commitments: installed and workspace governance files remain in sync
anti_overfit_checks: The model applies to any governed greenfield, brownfield, artifact, or handoff engagement.
next_safe_action: Require engagement governance validation before future material governed DFMS work.
